_note: Hand decisions for the ledger keys that name-match an external vocabulary. Every reuse target here was confirmed to resolve against its owner before being recorded — an asserted IRI is the failure this profile exists to avoid. Keys not listed follow the mechanical path: coin under tracepass:/voc/dpp/, cite the instrument the template records, attach the verified QUDT unit where one exists.

envelope._note: Not `characteristics` properties at all. These are attributes of the UNTP Product envelope — its parties and its facility — so they compose one level up. Every path below uses a UNTP property confirmed to resolve: name, registeredId, idScheme, registrationCountry, partyAddress, organisationWebsite, partyAlsoKnownAs on Party; id/registeredId/idScheme on Facility. `role` values come from UNTP's 20-value PartyRole code list.

envelopeNotes.authorisedRepresentative: UNTP's PartyRole list has no authorised-representative role. `serviceProvider` is the nearest fit and the ESPR/CPR capacity is stated on the party — a deliberate approximation, not an exact mapping.
envelopeNotes.producerRegistrationNumber: A national WEEE producer-register number. It is a registeredId whose idScheme names that register, not a coined property.
envelopeNotes.importerEoriNumber: DG TAXUD publishes no EORI vocabulary (data.europa.eu/resource/authority/eori is 404), but EORI is still a party identifier, not a product property. It goes on the importer's party as registeredId with idScheme naming the EORI register — reusing UNTP's structure without inventing a vocabulary nobody publishes.
envelopeNotes.countryOfOrigin: Duplicates what the envelope's countryOfProduction already carries. Coining a second country property would create two answers to one question.
envelopeNotes.economicOperatorIdentifier: An EORI or registration identifier of the operator placing the battery on the market — the same case as importerEoriNumber. Found by a description sweep, not by the key-name hints: the name contains neither 'importer' nor 'eori'.
envelopeNotes.uniqueOperatorId: A GLN or VAT number identifying the economic operator. Both are registered identifiers of a party, so idScheme names which register.
envelopeNotes.uniqueOperatorIdentifier: Same as uniqueOperatorId; the template describes it as the manufacturer/importer placing the product on the EU market.
envelopeNotes.retailerName: UNTP's PartyRole list includes `retailer`, so this is a party under that role rather than a coined product property.
envelopeNotes.supplierName: The tyre template's supplier IS the manufacturer per its own description.
envelopeNotes.supplierAddress: Registered address of that same party.
envelopeNotes.uniqueProductIdentifier: A GS1 Digital Link URI serving as the product's primary identifier — which is exactly what the UNTP envelope's `credentialSubject.id` carries. Declaring it again inside `characteristics` gives one product two identifiers and invites a producer to fill both. Steel's hand-authored example already omitted it while the schema still declared it; this makes that implicit judgement explicit.

coinedDespiteHint._note: Name-matched an external vocabulary but must still be coined, each for a stated reason. Recording WHY prevents a future pass from 'fixing' these into a reuse that does not hold.
coinedDespiteHint.manufacturerEmail: UNTP's Party models no email property. Confirmed against the published Party definition — it carries name, registeredId, idScheme, registrationCountry, partyAddress, organisationWebsite, partyAlsoKnownAs, industryCategory, and nothing for contact channels.
coinedDespiteHint.manufacturerPhone: Same as manufacturerEmail — UNTP Party has no phone property.
coinedDespiteHint.casNumber: CAS is the VALUE space, not the predicate. identifiers.org/cas:<n> resolves a specific SUBSTANCE (verified: 7439-92-1, 7440-43-9, 1163-19-5 all 200) — there is no CAS property IRI meaning 'has CAS number'. Coin the property; declare the value as a cas: IRI so the substance stays dereferenceable.
coinedDespiteHint.substanceName: A substance NAME is not an identifier and CAS does not model names as properties.
coinedDespiteHint.flameRetardantSubstances: An array of substance objects, each of which may carry a cas: value. The array property itself is ours.
coinedDespiteHint.substancesOfConcern: Same shape; appears in 4 categories, so one decision covers all four.

falsePositives._note: The ledger's externalHints are prompts, never answers. These matched a pattern and have nothing to do with the vocabulary it suggested. They take the ordinary mechanical path.
falsePositives.expansionSlots: Matched /lot/ inside 'slots'. It counts PCIe expansion slots — unrelated to GS1 batch/lot.
falsePositives.installationInstructions: Matched /installation/, which the hint reads as a production facility. It is a document telling an installer how to fit a construction product.
falsePositives.sparePartsWebsiteUrl: Matched /site/ inside 'Website'. It is a spare-parts ordering URL, not a facility.
falsePositives.gemstoneOrigin: Matched /origin/. It is the country a gemstone was mined in — geography, not a customs identifier.

standards._note: Owning standard for a coined term whose owner publishes no dereferenceable IRI. Each is taken from the field's own description in the template (or, for the EN 15804 impact indicators, from the indicator set they belong to) — never inferred from the key name alone. A key absent from this map has no external owner and is genuinely ours; that is a finding, not a gap.
standards.adpeMinerals: EN 15804+A2 (abiotic depletion potential, minerals and metals)
standards.lifeCycleModules: EN 15804+A2 (life-cycle module definitions A1-A3, C1-C4, D)
standards.en71TestResults: EN 71 (safety of toys: -1 mechanical, -2 flammability, -3 migration of elements)
standards.isoClassification: ISO 12944 (corrosivity categories for protective paint systems)
standards.totalVocEmissionUgM3: EN 16516 (determination of emissions into indoor air)
standards.fairminedCertified: Fairmined Standard (voluntary, artisanal and small-scale mining)
standards.gwpLuluc: EN 15804+A2 (global warming potential, land use and land-use change)
standards.applicableDurabilityStandard: EN durability/strength test standards (named per product family)
